segments_english.text: This subtopic looks like a forest of formulas, so let me hand you the one seed they all grow from.
Sum, difference, double, half, triple, product-to-sum, sum-to-product, every one of them is the same idea in a different costume.
The master key is the cosine difference formula: cosine of A minus B equals cosine A cosine B plus sine A sine B. Burn this one in.
Here's the family tree. Everything you'll ever need in this subtopic hangs off that single root at the top.
Watch how they grow. Replace B with minus B and you get cosine of A plus B. Use the cofunction shift, sine equals cosine of ninety minus the angle, and out fall sine of A plus or minus B.
Set B equal to A and you get the double-angle formulas. Halve the angle for half-angle. Add and subtract pairs and you get product-to-sum. One idea, eight costumes.
So the instruction is: don't memorise the list, learn the derivation. Under exam pressure you can rebuild any of them from cosine of A minus B in about twenty seconds, and it never fails you.

segments_hinglish.text: ये subtopic formulas का जंगल लगता है, so मैं आपको वो एक बीज देता हूँ जिससे सब उगते हैं.
Sum, difference, double, half, triple, product-to-sum, sum-to-product, हर एक वही idea है अलग costume में.
Master key है cosine difference formula: cosine of A minus B equals cosine A cosine B plus sine A sine B. इसे पक्का कर लीजिए.
ये रहा family tree. इस subtopic में जो कुछ चाहिए वो सब ऊपर के उस एक root से लटकता है.
देखिए कैसे उगते हैं. B को minus B से replace कीजिए और मिलता है cosine of A plus B. Cofunction shift use कीजिए, sine equals cosine of ninety minus angle, और निकल आते हैं sine of A plus or minus B.
B को A के बराबर कीजिए और मिलते हैं double-angle formulas. Angle आधा कीजिए half-angle के लिए. Pairs add और subtract कीजिए product-to-sum के लिए. एक idea, आठ costumes.
So instruction ये है: list रटिए मत, derivation सीखिए. Exam pressure में आप किसी को भी cosine of A minus B से करीब बीस seconds में rebuild कर सकते हैं, और ये कभी fail नहीं करता.

subtopic: 05 · Trigonometric Identities and Compound Angle Formulas
title: What a compound angle means — and why sin doesn't distribute

board_content.text: A compound angle is built from two others
$A+B$ or $A-B$. The naive guess $\sin(A+B)=\sin A+\sin B$ is flatly wrong.
Trig functions are not linear — they never distribute over a sum. This is the deepest error to kill early.
Two pushes combine into one
A sideways push $a\cos x$ and a forward push $b\sin x$ add to a single push of strength $R$ in one direction.

board_content.latex: a\cos x + b\sin x = R\cos(x-\alpha),\quad R=\sqrt{a^2+b^2}

board_content.text: So the maximum is $+R$ and the minimum is $-R$ \u2014 no calculus needed.

segments_english.text: Before the catalogue, let's be clear what a compound angle even is, and what it is not.
It's just an angle built from two others, A plus B or A minus B. And the tempting guess, that sine of A plus B equals sine A plus sine B, is simply false.
Test it: let A and B both be thirty degrees. Sine of sixty is root three over two, about zero point eight seven. But sine thirty plus sine thirty is one half plus one half, which is one. Not equal.
The lesson is deep: trig functions are not linear, they never distribute over a sum. Kill this instinct early and you avoid the most common error in the whole chapter.
Here's the intuition for the amplitude form, which we'll lean on.
Push a swing partly sideways, a cosine x, and partly forward, b sine x. The two combine into one single push, of strength R, in one combined direction.
That is, a cosine x plus b sine x equals R cosine of x minus alpha, where R is the square root of a squared plus b squared.
And because a cosine ranges between plus and minus one, the maximum of the whole thing is plus R and the minimum is minus R, no calculus required.

segments_hinglish.text: Catalogue से पहले, साफ़ कर लें compound angle है क्या, और क्या नहीं.
ये बस दो और angles से बना angle है, A plus B या A minus B. और tempting guess, कि sine of A plus B equals sine A plus sine B, बस ग़लत है.
Test कीजिए: A और B दोनों thirty degrees लीजिए. Sine of sixty है root three over two, करीब zero point eight seven. पर sine thirty plus sine thirty है one half plus one half, यानी one. बराबर नहीं.
सबक गहरा है: trig functions linear नहीं हैं, वो sum पर कभी distribute नहीं करतीं. इस instinct को जल्दी मार दीजिए और पूरे chapter की सबसे common ग़लती से बच जाइए.
अब amplitude form का intuition, जिस पर हम टिकेंगे.
एक swing को partly sideways धकेलिए, a cosine x, और partly forward, b sine x. दोनों मिलकर एक single push बनते हैं, strength R का, एक combined direction में.
यानी a cosine x plus b sine x equals R cosine of x minus alpha, जहाँ R है square root of a squared plus b squared.
और चूँकि a cosine plus और minus one के बीच रहता है, पूरी चीज़ का maximum plus R और minimum minus R है, calculus की ज़रूरत नहीं.

subtopic: 05 · Trigonometric Identities and Compound Angle Formulas
title: Sum and difference formulas, with the sign mnemonic

board_content.text: Compound angle: sum and difference
Sign mnemonic: cosine flips the sign, sine follows the sign, tangent's denominator is opposite the numerator.

board_content.caption: cos(A−B): equal chords on the unit circle give the master formula

board_content.text: Useful products of compound angles

segments_english.text: Here's the first block of the catalogue, the sum and difference formulas.
For cosine of A plus or minus B: cosine A cosine B, then minus or plus sine A sine B. The sign is opposite to the one inside.
For sine of A plus or minus B: sine A cosine B, then plus or minus cosine A sine B. The sign matches the one inside.
For tangent of A plus or minus B: tangent A plus or minus tangent B, all over one minus or plus tangent A tangent B.
One clean mnemonic ties them: cosine flips the sign, sine follows the sign, and for tangent the denominator's sign is opposite the numerator's.

And this is where the master formula comes from, geometrically: two equal chords on the unit circle, one spanning A to B and one spanning A minus B back to the point one, zero. Equal central angles force equal chords, and equating their squared lengths gives cosine of A minus B.
Two products worth memorising.
Cosine of A plus B times cosine of A minus B equals cosine squared A minus sine squared B.
And sine of A plus B times sine of A minus B equals sine squared A minus sine squared B.

segments_hinglish.text: Catalogue का पहला block, sum और difference formulas.
Cosine of A plus or minus B के लिए: cosine A cosine B, फिर minus या plus sine A sine B. Sign अंदर वाले के opposite है.
Sine of A plus or minus B के लिए: sine A cosine B, फिर plus या minus cosine A sine B. Sign अंदर वाले से match करता है.
Tangent of A plus or minus B के लिए: tangent A plus or minus tangent B, पूरे over one minus या plus tangent A tangent B.
एक clean mnemonic इन्हें जोड़ता है: cosine sign flip करता है, sine sign follow करता है, और tangent में denominator का sign numerator के opposite होता है.

और master formula यहीं से आता है, geometrically: unit circle पर दो equal chords, एक A से B तक और एक A minus B से वापस point one, zero तक. Equal central angles equal chords force करते हैं, और उनकी squared lengths बराबर करने से मिलता है cosine of A minus B.
दो products याद रखने लायक़.
Cosine of A plus B times cosine of A minus B equals cosine squared A minus sine squared B.
और sine of A plus B times sine of A minus B equals sine squared A minus sine squared B.

subtopic: 05 · Trigonometric Identities and Compound Angle Formulas
title: Double, half, triple and the t-substitution

board_content.text: Double-angle
Half-angle / power reduction
The t = tan(A/2) substitution
Triple-angle

segments_english.text: Set B equal to A in the sum formulas and the double-angle family drops out.
Sine two A is two sine A cosine A, and tangent two A is two tangent A over one minus tangent squared A.
Cosine two A has three faces: cosine squared A minus sine squared A, or two cosine squared A minus one, or one minus two sine squared A. Choose whichever matches what you're given.
Rearranging cosine two A gives the half-angle, or power-reduction, forms.
One plus cosine A is two cosine squared of A over two; one minus cosine A is two sine squared of A over two, the workhorses for integrals later.
Next, the t-substitution, with t as tangent of A over two.

It turns any rational trig expression into a rational function of t: sine A is two t over one plus t squared, cosine A is one minus t squared over one plus t squared, tangent A is two t over one minus t squared.
And the triple-angle pair, built from three A equals two A plus A.
Sine three A is three sine A minus four sine cubed A, and cosine three A is four cosine cubed A minus three cosine A.

One plus cosine A है two cosine squared of A over two; one minus cosine A है two sine squared of A over two, बाद में integrals के workhorses.
अगला, t-substitution, t को tangent of A over two लेकर.

ये किसी भी rational trig expression को t के rational function में बदल देता है: sine A है two t over one plus t squared, cosine A one minus t squared over one plus t squared, tangent A two t over one minus t squared.
और triple-angle pair, three A equals two A plus A से बना.
Sine three A है three sine A minus four sine cubed A, और cosine three A है four cosine cubed A minus three cosine A.

board_content.text: The condition A + B + C = π is used at the very first step — drop it and the identity is false.

segments_english.text: Example seven: prove cosine twenty times cosine forty times cosine eighty equals one eighth.
The trick is deliberate: multiply and divide by twice sine twenty, then cascade the double-angle identity, twice sine theta cosine theta is sine two theta.

Each step doubles the angle, giving sine one sixty over eight sine twenty; since sine one sixty equals sine twenty, it collapses to one eighth. That opening move is a signature technique you must know, not something you pattern-match.
Example eight is a conditional identity in a triangle: given A plus B plus C is pi, prove the sum of tangents equals the product.

From A plus B equals pi minus C, take tangents: tangent of A plus B is minus tangent C, so the sum formula gives tangent A plus tangent B, over one minus tangent A tangent B, equal to minus tangent C.
Cross-multiply and rearrange, and you land exactly on tangent A plus tangent B plus tangent C equals tangent A tangent B tangent C.
The key warning: the condition A plus B plus C equals pi is used at the very first step. Without it the identity is simply false, the scope trap examiners love.

हर step angle दुगुना करता है, देता sine one sixty over eight sine twenty; चूँकि sine one sixty equals sine twenty, ये one eighth में collapse हो जाता है. वो शुरुआती move एक signature technique है जो आपको पता होनी चाहिए, pattern-match करने की चीज़ नहीं.

A plus B equals pi minus C से, tangents लीजिए: tangent of A plus B है minus tangent C, so sum formula देता tangent A plus tangent B, over one minus tangent A tangent B, बराबर minus tangent C.

subtopic: 05 · Trigonometric Identities and Compound Angle Formulas
title: Pitfalls in identities and compound angles

board_content.text: Identity traps
#1 Signature trap: the cosine/tangent sign flip. cos(A+B) takes minus; cos(A−B) takes plus. Cosine disagrees with the angle sign; sine agrees.
#2 Assuming distribution: $\sin(A+B)\ne\sin A+\sin B$. Always use the formula.
#3 Wrong $\cos 2A$ form. Given $\sin A$ use $1-2\sin^2 A$; given $\cos A$ use $2\cos^2 A-1$.
#4 Dropping the leading 2 in product-to-sum, and the leading minus in cos C − cos D.
#5 Amplitude is $\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$, never $a+b$. #6 Conditional identities hold only when A + B + C = \u03c0.
Golden rule: reconstruct from cos(A−B); watch every ±; amplitude is √(a²+b²).

segments_english.text: Six traps in the engine room, mostly structural, not arithmetic.

The signature trap: the sign flip in cosine and tangent. Cosine of A plus B takes a minus, cosine of A minus B takes a plus, so cosine disagrees with the angle's sign. Sine, by contrast, agrees. Get this backwards and everything downstream breaks.
Second, assuming distribution. Sine of A plus B is not sine A plus sine B. Trig functions are not linear, always reach for the formula.
Third, picking the wrong face of cosine two A. If you're given sine A, use one minus two sine squared A; if given cosine A, use two cosine squared A minus one. Match the form to what you have.
Fourth, dropping little pieces: the leading two in the product-to-sum formulas, and the leading minus in cosine C minus cosine D. Both are part of the formula.

Fifth, the amplitude of a sine plus b cosine is the square root of a squared plus b squared, never a plus b. And sixth, conditional identities like the tangent sum only hold when A plus B plus C is pi.
The golden rule: reconstruct everything from cosine of A minus B, watch every plus-or-minus, and remember the amplitude is root a squared plus b squared.

segments_hinglish.text: Engine room में छह traps, ज़्यादातर structural, arithmetic नहीं.

Signature trap: cosine और tangent में sign flip. Cosine of A plus B minus लेता है, cosine of A minus B plus लेता है, so cosine angle के sign से disagree करता है. Sine, इसके उलट, agree करता है. इसे उल्टा किया तो आगे सब टूट जाता है.
दूसरा, distribution मानना. Sine of A plus B, sine A plus sine B नहीं है. Trig functions linear नहीं, हमेशा formula उठाइए.
तीसरा, cosine two A का ग़लत चेहरा चुनना. अगर sine A दिया है, one minus two sine squared A use कीजिए; cosine A दिया है तो two cosine squared A minus one. Form को जो है उससे match कीजिए.
चौथा, छोटे टुकड़े छोड़ना: product-to-sum में leading two, और cosine C minus cosine D में leading minus. दोनों formula का हिस्सा हैं.
पाँचवाँ, a sine plus b cosine का amplitude है square root of a squared plus b squared, कभी a plus b नहीं. और छठा, conditional identities जैसे tangent sum सिर्फ़ तभी valid जब A plus B plus C is pi.
Golden rule: सब कुछ cosine of A minus B से reconstruct कीजिए, हर plus-or-minus देखिए, और याद रखिए amplitude है root a squared plus b squared.

board_content.text: Two layers of answer
A principal solution lies in $[0,2\pi)$. For $\sin\theta=\tfrac12$ there are two: $\tfrac{\pi}{6}$ and $\tfrac{5\pi}{6}$.
Like a train timetable: not one arrival time, but the whole recurring schedule, with n counting the laps.
The job is never to find a solution — it is to describe every solution in one stroke.

segments_english.text: A trig equation asks: for which angles does this statement hold? And the answer is almost never a single number.
Because trig functions repeat forever, if one angle solves sine theta equals one half, then adding any whole number of full turns gives another solution, and so does that angle's mirror partner.
See it on the circle: the line y equals one half cuts the sine at two places in the first lap, at pi over six and five pi over six, and each of those repeats every two pi.
So think in two layers.
A principal solution lives in the first lap, zero up to two pi. For sine theta equals one half there are exactly two: pi over six and five pi over six.
The general solution packages every answer with an integer n: theta equals n pi plus minus one to the n, times pi over six.
It's exactly a train timetable. You don't answer when is a train here with one time, you give the recurring schedule, and n counts the laps.
So the real job is never just to find a solution, it's to describe all of them in a single formula.

segments_hinglish.text: एक trig equation पूछती है: किन angles पर ये statement टिकता है? और answer लगभग कभी एक number नहीं होता.

चूँकि trig functions हमेशा repeat होते हैं, अगर एक angle sine theta equals one half solve करता है, तो कोई भी whole number of full turns जोड़ने से दूसरा solution मिलता है, और उस angle का mirror partner भी.
Circle पर देखिए: line y equals one half पहले lap में sine को दो जगह काटती है, pi over six और five pi over six पर, और हर एक every two pi repeat होता है.
So दो layers में सोचिए.
एक principal solution पहले lap में रहता है, zero से two pi तक. Sine theta equals one half के लिए बिल्कुल दो हैं: pi over six और five pi over six.
General solution हर answer को integer n के साथ package करता है: theta equals n pi plus minus one to the n, times pi over six.
ये बिल्कुल train timetable है. आप ये नहीं बताते कि train कब है एक time से, आप recurring schedule देते हैं, और n laps गिनता है.
So असली काम कभी सिर्फ़ एक solution ढूँढना नहीं, सबको एक single formula में describe करना है.

subtopic: 06 · Trigonometric Equations and Solutions
title: The two great dangers: dividing and squaring

board_content.text: Losing roots by dividing
If you cancel $\cos\theta$ from $\sin\theta\cos\theta=\cos\theta$, you silently throw away every solution where $\cos\theta=0$.
Cancelling assumes the thing you cancel is non-zero — but here it can be zero. Factor, never divide.
Gaining roots by squaring
Squaring both sides can make a false equation look true, since $(-1)^2=1^2$.

board_content.latex: \sin x + \cos x = 1 \xrightarrow{\text{square}} \sin 2x = 0,\ \text{but } x=\pi \text{ fails the original}

board_content.text: Every solution from a squared equation must be checked back in the original.
These two are the signature traps — both are conceptual gaps, not careless slips.

segments_english.text: Two dangers cause almost every wrong answer in this subtopic, and both are conceptual.
The first is losing roots by dividing. Suppose you have sine theta cosine theta equals cosine theta, and you cancel cosine theta from both sides.
The moment you cancel, you silently throw away every solution where cosine theta is zero.
Cancelling secretly assumes the thing you cancel is non-zero. But here it can be zero, that's exactly the case you just deleted. So factor, and set each factor to zero, never divide.
The second danger is gaining roots by squaring. Squaring both sides can make a false statement look true, because minus one squared equals one squared.

Watch: sine x plus cosine x equals one. Square it and you get sine two x equals zero, which includes x equal to pi. But sine pi plus cosine pi is minus one, not one, so x equal to pi is a fake, an extraneous root.
So every candidate that comes out of a squared equation must be checked back in the original, and the fakes discarded.
These are the two signature traps of the whole subtopic, and notice, they're gaps in understanding, not careless arithmetic.

segments_hinglish.text: दो dangers इस subtopic के लगभग हर ग़लत answer की वजह हैं, और दोनों conceptual हैं.
पहला है divide करके roots खोना. मान लीजिए sine theta cosine theta equals cosine theta है, और आप दोनों तरफ़ से cosine theta cancel कर देते हैं.
जिस पल आप cancel करते हैं, आप चुपचाप हर वो solution फेंक देते हैं जहाँ cosine theta zero है.
Cancel करना चुपके से मानता है कि जो cancel कर रहे हैं वो non-zero है. पर यहाँ वो zero हो सकता है, यही case आपने अभी delete किया. So factor कीजिए, हर factor को zero रखिए, divide कभी नहीं.
दूसरा danger है square करके roots पाना. दोनों तरफ़ square करना झूठे statement को सच दिखा सकता है, क्योंकि minus one squared equals one squared.

देखिए: sine x plus cosine x equals one. Square कीजिए और मिलता है sine two x equals zero, जिसमें x equal to pi शामिल है. पर sine pi plus cosine pi है minus one, one नहीं, so x equal to pi नक़ली है, extraneous root.
So squared equation से निकला हर candidate original में check होना चाहिए, और नक़ली हटा दीजिए.
ये पूरे subtopic के दो signature traps हैं, और ध्यान दीजिए, ये समझ की कमी हैं, careless arithmetic नहीं.

subtopic: 06 · Trigonometric Equations and Solutions
title: The master solution formulas and the root-validity check

board_content.text: Zero cases
The three master general solutions
Linear form and solvability
Checklist: keep n; restore roots lost to division; back-check after squaring; drop out-of-domain roots. (n ∈ ℤ)

segments_english.text: Here is the short, fixed list that solves the whole subtopic. Start with the zero cases.
Sine theta is zero at whole multiples of pi; cosine theta at odd multiples of pi over two; tangent theta at whole multiples of pi.
Now the three master general solutions, one per function.
For sine theta equals sine alpha: theta is n pi plus minus one to the n, times alpha.
For cosine theta equals cosine alpha: theta is two n pi plus or minus alpha; and for tangent theta equals tangent alpha: theta is n pi plus alpha. Never borrow another function's form.
One more covers all squared cases: sine squared, cosine squared, or tangent squared equal to the same of alpha gives theta equals n pi plus or minus alpha.
Then the linear form and its solvability test.

Rewrite a cosine theta plus b sine theta as R cosine of theta minus alpha equals c; it's solvable only if the size of c is at most the square root of a squared plus b squared, otherwise there is no solution.

And run the root-validity checklist every time: keep the integer n, restore any roots lost to division, back-check every candidate after squaring, and drop any out-of-domain root. Throughout, n is an integer.

segments_hinglish.text: पूरे subtopic को solve करने वाली short, fixed list यहाँ है. Zero cases से शुरू कीजिए.
Sine theta zero है pi के whole multiples पर; cosine theta odd multiples of pi over two पर; tangent theta pi के whole multiples पर.
अब तीन master general solutions, हर function के लिए एक.
Sine theta equals sine alpha के लिए: theta है n pi plus minus one to the n, times alpha.
Cosine theta equals cosine alpha के लिए: theta है two n pi plus or minus alpha; और tangent theta equals tangent alpha के लिए: theta है n pi plus alpha. दूसरे function का form कभी मत उधार लीजिए.
एक और सारे squared cases cover करता है: sine squared, cosine squared, या tangent squared, alpha के same के बराबर, देता theta equals n pi plus or minus alpha.
फिर linear form और उसका solvability test.
a cosine theta plus b sine theta को R cosine of theta minus alpha equals c लिखिए; ये तभी solvable है जब c का size square root of a squared plus b squared से ज़्यादा ना हो, वरना no solution.

और हर बार root-validity checklist चलाइए: integer n रखिए, division से खोए roots restore कीजिए, squaring के बाद हर candidate back-check कीजिए, और कोई out-of-domain root हटाइए. पूरे में, n एक integer है.

subtopic: 06 · Trigonometric Equations and Solutions
title: Principal solutions, a general solution, and a quadratic

board_content.text: Example 1 — principal solutions of sin x = 1/2
Example 2 — general solution of cos x = −1/2
Example 3 — quadratic in sin x: 2sin²x + sinx − 1 = 0
Factor as $(2\sin x - 1)(\sin x + 1)=0$, so $\sin x=\tfrac12$ or $\sin x=-1$.

segments_english.text: Three foundational solves.

First, principal solutions of sine x equals one half. Sine is positive in the first and second quadrants, so within one lap we get x equals pi over six, and x equals pi minus pi over six, which is five pi over six.
Second, the general solution of cosine x equals minus one half. Minus one half is cosine of two pi over three, so by the cosine formula, x equals two n pi plus or minus two pi over three.
Third, a quadratic in sine x: two sine squared x plus sine x minus one equals zero.
Treat sine x as the variable and factor: two sine x minus one, times sine x plus one, equals zero. So sine x is one half, or sine x is minus one.
From sine x equals one half, x is n pi plus minus one to the n times pi over six. From sine x equals minus one, x is four n minus one, times pi over two.
The habit to build: reduce every equation to sine equals sine, cosine equals cosine, or tangent equals tangent, then just quote the matching master formula.

segments_hinglish.text: तीन foundational solves.
पहला, sine x equals one half के principal solutions. Sine पहले और दूसरे quadrant में positive है, so एक lap में मिलता है x equals pi over six, और x equals pi minus pi over six, यानी five pi over six.
दूसरा, cosine x equals minus one half का general solution. Minus one half है cosine of two pi over three, so cosine formula से, x equals two n pi plus or minus two pi over three.
तीसरा, sine x में एक quadratic: two sine squared x plus sine x minus one equals zero.
Sine x को variable मानकर factor कीजिए: two sine x minus one, times sine x plus one, equals zero. So sine x है one half, या sine x है minus one.
Sine x equals one half से, x है n pi plus minus one to the n times pi over six. Sine x equals minus one से, x है four n minus one, times pi over two.
जो आदत बनानी है: हर equation को sine equals sine, cosine equals cosine, या tangent equals tangent में reduce कीजिए, फिर बस matching master formula quote कीजिए.

subtopic: 06 · Trigonometric Equations and Solutions
title: The linear form, and factoring instead of dividing

board_content.text: Example 4 — solve √3 cos x + sin x = 1
$R=\sqrt{3+1}=2$, $\tan\alpha=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt3}\Rightarrow\alpha=\tfrac{\pi}{6}$. So $\cos(x-\tfrac{\pi}{6})=\tfrac12=\cos\tfrac{\pi}{3}$.
Example 5 — factor, don't divide: sin 2x = sin x
$\sin x = 0 \Rightarrow x=n\pi$; $\cos x=\tfrac12 \Rightarrow x=2n\pi\pm\tfrac{\pi}{3}$.
Dividing by sin x would erase the entire x = nπ family — the signature trap.

segments_english.text: Two workhorses: the linear form and the factor-don't-divide discipline.

Example four: solve root three cosine x plus sine x equals one. Here a is root three and b is one, so R is the square root of three plus one, which is two, and tangent alpha is one over root three, so alpha is pi over six.
Rewrite as two cosine of x minus pi over six equals one, that is cosine of x minus pi over six equals one half, which is cosine pi over three.

So x minus pi over six equals two n pi plus or minus pi over three, giving x equals two n pi plus pi over two, or x equals two n pi minus pi over six. And the size of c, one, is at most R, two, so solutions do exist.

Example five drives home factoring. Solve sine two x equals sine x. Move everything over: two sine x cosine x minus sine x equals zero, then factor out sine x to get sine x times two cosine x minus one equals zero.
So either sine x is zero, giving x equals n pi, or cosine x is one half, giving x equals two n pi plus or minus pi over three.
If instead you had divided both sides by sine x, you would have erased the entire x equals n pi family. That is the signature trap, factor, never divide.

segments_hinglish.text: दो workhorses: linear form और factor-don't-divide discipline.

Example चार: solve कीजिए root three cosine x plus sine x equals one. यहाँ a है root three और b one, so R है square root of three plus one, यानी two, और tangent alpha है one over root three, so alpha है pi over six.
फिर से लिखिए two cosine of x minus pi over six equals one, यानी cosine of x minus pi over six equals one half, जो cosine pi over three है.

So x minus pi over six equals two n pi plus or minus pi over three, देता x equals two n pi plus pi over two, या x equals two n pi minus pi over six. और c का size, one, R यानी two से ज़्यादा नहीं, so solutions मौजूद हैं.

Example पाँच factoring पक्का करता है. Solve कीजिए sine two x equals sine x. सब एक तरफ़ लाइए: two sine x cosine x minus sine x equals zero, फिर sine x बाहर factor कीजिए, मिलता sine x times two cosine x minus one equals zero.
So या तो sine x zero है, देता x equals n pi, या cosine x one half है, देता x equals two n pi plus or minus pi over three.
अगर इसके बजाय आपने दोनों तरफ़ sine x से divide किया होता, आप पूरी x equals n pi family मिटा देते. यही signature trap है, factor, divide कभी नहीं.

subtopic: 06 · Trigonometric Equations and Solutions
title: The squaring trap done right, and a range squeeze

board_content.text: Example 6 — solve sin x + cos x = 1 (without squaring)
Amplitude form: $\sin x+\cos x=\sqrt2\,\sin(x+\tfrac{\pi}{4})$, so $\sin(x+\tfrac{\pi}{4})=\tfrac{1}{\sqrt2}=\sin\tfrac{\pi}{4}$.
Squaring instead gives sin 2x = 0, which admits x = π — but sinπ + cosπ = −1. Back-checking removes it.
Example 7 — range squeeze: 2sin²x + sin²2x = 2
With $\sin^2 2x = 4\sin^2 x\cos^2 x$ and $s=\sin^2 x$: $2s+4s(1-s)=2 \Rightarrow (2s-1)(s-1)=0$.

segments_english.text: The finale: how to beat the squaring trap, and a neat substitution.

Example six: solve sine x plus cosine x equals one. The safe route avoids squaring entirely, use the amplitude form. Sine x plus cosine x is root two times sine of x plus pi over four, so sine of x plus pi over four equals one over root two, which is sine pi over four.
Solving that gives x equals two n pi, or x equals two n pi plus pi over two. Clean, with no fakes.

Contrast the squaring route: square the original and you get sine two x equals zero, which admits x equal to pi. But sine pi plus cosine pi is minus one, not one, so pi is extraneous. Only back-checking removes it, which is why the amplitude form is safer.
Example seven, a range squeeze: two sine squared x plus sine squared two x equals two.

Write sine squared two x as four sine squared x cosine squared x, and let s be sine squared x. Then two s plus four s times one minus s equals two, which tidies to two s minus one, times s minus one, equals zero.

So s is one half or s is one. Sine squared x equals one half gives x equals n pi plus or minus pi over four; sine squared x equals one means cosine x is zero, giving x equals two n plus one, times pi over two.

segments_hinglish.text: Finale: squaring trap को कैसे हराएँ, और एक neat substitution.

Example छह: solve कीजिए sine x plus cosine x equals one. Safe route squaring से पूरी तरह बचता है, amplitude form use कीजिए. Sine x plus cosine x है root two times sine of x plus pi over four, so sine of x plus pi over four equals one over root two, जो sine pi over four है.
इसे solve करने पर x equals two n pi, या x equals two n pi plus pi over two. साफ़, कोई नक़ली नहीं.

Squaring route से तुलना: original को square कीजिए और मिलता sine two x equals zero, जिसमें x equal to pi है. पर sine pi plus cosine pi है minus one, one नहीं, so pi extraneous है. सिर्फ़ back-checking इसे हटाता है, इसीलिए amplitude form safer है.
Example सात, एक range squeeze: two sine squared x plus sine squared two x equals two.

Sine squared two x को four sine squared x cosine squared x लिखिए, और s को sine squared x लीजिए. तो two s plus four s times one minus s equals two, जो साफ़ होकर two s minus one, times s minus one, equals zero बनता है.

So s है one half या s है one. Sine squared x equals one half देता x equals n pi plus or minus pi over four; sine squared x equals one मतलब cosine x zero, देता x equals two n plus one, times pi over two.

subtopic: 06 · Trigonometric Equations and Solutions
title: Pitfalls in solving trig equations

board_content.text: Equation traps
#1 Signature trap: dividing by a trig factor and losing roots. Never cancel sin x or cos x — factor and set each factor to zero.
#2 Squaring and keeping extraneous roots. Every candidate from a squared step must be checked in the original equation.
#3 Mixing the families. Sine: $n\pi+(-1)^n\alpha$; cosine: $2n\pi\pm\alpha$; tangent: $n\pi+\alpha$. Never borrow another's form.
#4 Giving only principal solutions when 'general' is asked — the integer n is mandatory.
#5 Ignoring solvability: if $|c|>\sqrt{a^2+b^2}$, declare 'no solution'. #6 Drop roots where tan, sec, cot or csc is undefined.
Golden rules: factor (never divide); back-check after squaring; keep the n; match the right family.

segments_english.text: Six traps that decide the equations marks.
The signature trap: dividing by a trig factor and losing roots. Never cancel sine x or cosine x, because the thing you cancel might be zero. Factor instead, and set each factor to zero.
Second, squaring and keeping extraneous roots. Squaring can manufacture false solutions, so every candidate that came through a squared step must be checked back in the original equation.

Third, mixing up the solution families. Sine gives n pi plus minus one to the n times alpha; cosine gives two n pi plus or minus alpha; tangent gives n pi plus alpha. Each function has its own form, never borrow another's.
Fourth, giving only principal solutions when the question asks for the general one. The integer n is mandatory; drop it and you lose infinitely many answers.

Fifth, ignoring solvability of the linear form. If the size of c exceeds the square root of a squared plus b squared, just declare no solution instead of grinding. And sixth, discard any root where tangent, secant, cotangent or cosecant is undefined.
The golden rules for the whole subtopic: factor, never divide; back-check after squaring; keep the n; and match the right family to the right function.

segments_hinglish.text: Equations के marks तय करने वाले छह traps.
Signature trap: trig factor से divide करके roots खोना. Sine x या cosine x कभी cancel मत कीजिए, क्योंकि जो cancel कर रहे हैं वो zero हो सकता है. इसके बजाय factor कीजिए, और हर factor को zero रखिए.
दूसरा, square करके extraneous roots रखना. Squaring झूठे solutions बना सकता है, so squared step से आया हर candidate original equation में back-check होना चाहिए.

तीसरा, solution families mix करना. Sine देता n pi plus minus one to the n times alpha; cosine देता two n pi plus or minus alpha; tangent देता n pi plus alpha. हर function का अपना form, दूसरे का कभी उधार नहीं.
चौथा, सिर्फ़ principal solutions देना जब सवाल general माँगे. Integer n ज़रूरी है; छोड़िए और infinitely many answers खो जाते हैं.

पाँचवाँ, linear form की solvability ignore करना. अगर c का size square root of a squared plus b squared से ज़्यादा है, बस no solution घोषित कीजिए grind करने के बजाय. और छठा, जहाँ tangent, secant, cotangent या cosecant undefined हो वो root हटाइए.
पूरे subtopic के golden rules: factor, divide कभी नहीं; squaring के बाद back-check; n रखिए; और सही family को सही function से match कीजिए.

title: Chapter cheat sheet — golden rules and traps

board_content.text: Fast-recall golden rules
Angles: any arc / sector / calculus formula assumes radians. Convert first, always.
Functions: magnitude from the identity, sign from the quadrant — always two steps. Range-check every answer.
Allied angles: odd multiple of 90° ⇒ swap to co-function; sign from the quadrant via ASTC.
Graphs: divide (don't multiply) for the period; tangent's period is π; include the vertical shift in the range.
Identities: reconstruct everything from cos(A−B); watch every ±; amplitude is √(a²+b²), never a+b.
Equations: factor (never divide); back-check after squaring; keep the n; match the right solution family.
If a final sin or cos exceeds 1 in magnitude, or a period looks multiplied not divided — stop and recheck.
